title: Bibi’s Iran Goals Are Not Necessarily Trump’s Iran Goals
author: Spencer Ackerman
content:

An unjustifiable, illegal war of aggression against Iran has united the United
States and Israel. For now.

The triumphalism in Washington and Jerusalem is extreme after Saturday
morning's surprise assassination of Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamanei
inaugurated the largest and most horrifying US military misadventure since the
2003 Iraq War. But it conceals the sources of major divergence between the US
and Israel over the most important and least defined questions of the war: the
endgame - and what comes next.

It would be a mistake to overstate President Donald**** Trump's coherence over
what the US objectives are. Announcing the war early Saturday morning, he told
the Iranian people that "when we finish" bombing, "take over your government."
But he offered the Iranians no guarantees, making regime change seem [like a
stretch goal](https://www.forever-wars.com/regime-change-in-iran-terms-and-
conditions-apply/). Then he offered "total immunity" to the Islamic
Revolutionary Guard Corps and other security forces that have the blood of
Iranian protesters on their hands.

[Trump's weekend media blitz](https://www.foreignexchanges.news/p/iran-war-
roundup-march-1-2026) added to the strategic confusion. Trump spoke about
potential "off-ramps" from the war and into negotiation - this, _after_
assassinating Khamanei - and also of perhaps "go[ing] long and tak[ing] over
the whole thing." Sometimes he presented his aims as decisive, to end the
never-quite-defined "threat" - a threat, that is, from a nonexistent nuclear-
weapons program and a missile arsenal that cannot remotely reach the United
States. Other times, Trump phrased his aims as a leverage ploy, with the war
"end[ing] in two or three days and tell[ing] the Iranians: 'See you again in a
few years if you start rebuilding.'" Or the war will last "[four
weeks](https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/trump-says-conflict-with-
iran-could-last-four-weeks-daily-mail-reports-2026-03-01/)." Or the war might,
as Trump signaled to the _New York Post_ on Monday, [require ground
troops](https://nypost.com/2026/03/02/us-news/trump-wont-rule-out-sending-us-
troops-into-iran-if-necessary-tells-the-post-i-dont-care-about-polling/), even
though its operations are "ahead of schedule."

There you have it: the Trump administration can and cannot live with the
continuation of the Islamic Republic. We have achieved Schroedinger's Forever
War. The experience of Venezuela, where a swift January operation kidnapped
Nicolas Maduro and then - for now - the post-Maduro government of Delcy
Rodriguez does his extractive bidding, is [shaping his approach to
Iran](https://www.thenation.com/article/world/trump-war-on-terror-dhs/). It
should alarm everyone but surprise no one that Trump has taken the US to war
without an endgame.

But there is something reliable to trust in the morass of Trump's declarations
on the war: the incentive for it not to last long. Trump is caught in the same
audience trap that caught George W. Bush in Iraq and Barack Obama in
Afghanistan. To Tehran, he must speak in the language of resolve, of a war
which will last as long as necessary to satisfy him, whatever that may mean.
But to America, he must speak in the language of limits, to convince a
domestic audience that he is not speedrunning the same Middle East
misadventures as his predecessors.

Israel, however, does _not_ want a quick war. And it definitely does not want
an indecisive one.

For Benjamin Netanyahu, a dream is in the balance: a dream of Israel's prime
regional adversary being crushed by Israeli might. His second and third
premierships have been defined by pressuring Washington to inflict as much
pain on Iran and eschew as much diplomacy with it as possible. After October
7, when it became clear that first Joe Biden and then Trump would aid and not
hinder the genocide of Gaza, his regional ambitions expanded. In 2024, Israel
assaulted Hamas, Hezbollah, and Iranian figures everywhere from Beirut to
Tehran, then seized territory in Syria once the Iran-backed Bashar Assad lost
the Syrian civil war. In last year's Twelve-Day War, Netanyahu became the
first Israeli PM ever to jointly conduct offensive military operations with
the United States - something every prior US president avoided for fear of
provoking the Muslim world. With adversary after adversary pummeled, Israel
sees this moment as its best chance to shift the balance of Middle Eastern
power durably in its favor. Netanyahu posted on Sunday that [he had waited 40
years](https://x.com/netanyahu/status/2028134104751804621?s=46) to "strike the
terrorist regime squarely in the hip."

Israel's endgame is as clear as it gets: the end of the Islamic Republic. It
and its allies have been unsubtle about letting it be known that [the Mossad
has extensive intelligence penetration](https://www.middleeasteye.net/news/we-
want-change-not-destruction-iranian-protesters-reject-us-israeli-interference)
in Iran. In addition to [backing the long-exiled son of the
Shah](https://www.haaretz.com/israel-news/security-aviation/2025-10-03/ty-
article-magazine/.premium/the-israeli-influence-operation-in-iran-pushing-to-
reinstate-the-shah-monarchy/00000199-9f12-df33-a5dd-9f770d7a0000), Israel's
messaging to the Iranian people has gone beyond the regime-change
encouragement issued by Trump. Netanyahu delivered a Persian-language message
on Sunday that emphasized the ["hour of freedom" at hand for Iran's many
ethnic minorities](https://www.eurasiareview.com/02032026-your-moment-has-
come-netanyahu-delivers-persian-message-urging-iranians/). Particularly with a
United States that does not wish to be responsible for an Iraq-style
occupation, this represents a step toward the Syriafication of Iran, most
likely through proxy forces. An Iran of 90 million people and great internal
and geographic diversity will not be able to challenge Israeli regional power
if it is mired in state collapse and civil war. The _Jerusalem Post_ has mused
openly about a "[federalized or partitioned
Iran](https://www.jpost.com/opinion/article-858111?ref=forever-wars.com)"
post-Islamic Republic.

An Iran in chaos, however, is a formula for drawing the United States in
deeper, not letting Washington get out and move on.

While world governments have proven their enormous willingness to ignore
internal bloodletting, a world still dependent on hydrocarbons - and the
[Chinese in particular](https://www.reuters.com/business/energy/chinas-heavy-
reliance-iranian-oil-imports-2026-01-13/) - cannot permit massive reserves of
its most important and globalized commodity to remain offline. Nor can it
tolerate the prospect of chaos near the Strait of Hormuz from permitting oil
shipments from the Gulf countries; or even the higher prices that come as
insurers balk at the risk of traversing the strait. The Gulf countries will
look to the US for economic and security protection and make US reluctance
costly, as Barack Obama learned. Regional governments will balk at absorbing
an Iranian migrant wave.

The Iraq War also instructs us that the war will create contingencies that we
cannot yet foresee that will entangle Washington even more deeply. Donald "I
don't do quagmires" Rumsfeld also thought he could get out of Iraq quickly.
That lesson should haunt [Vice President JD
Vance](https://www.washingtonpost.com/politics/2026/02/26/vance-no-chance-us-
will-be-drawn-out-war-middle-east/), whose presidential aspirations could go
the way of Kamala Harris, John Kerry, Hubert Humphrey, and others associated
with unpopular wars.

Doubtless the architects of this unfolding catastrophe, in Washington and
Jerusalem, will attempt to obscure the divergences in their goals. But the
longer their war goes on, [killing more
schoolchildren](https://news.un.org/en/story/2026/03/1167063) and [bombing
more hospitals](https://www.aljazeera.com/news/2026/3/2/iran-demands-
international-action-after-attacks-impact-hospitals-schools), the less tenable
that will be. No one could possibly shed any tears over Israeli and American
warmongers ensnaring themselves in a trap of their choosing. It is not for
their sake that people worldwide must pressure their governments for an end to
this latest insane war.
